claim: Tcf7l1a acts cell-autonomously to specify the eye field in zebrafish.
source: In this study, we show that Tcf7l1a is one such transcription factor that acts cell-autonomously to specify the eye field in zebrafish.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from cell transplantation experiments shown in Figure 3, where wildtype cells transplanted into MZtcf7l1a-/- hosts recovered rx3 expression, and MZtcf7l1a-/- cells in wildtype hosts showed reduced rx3 expression.

claim: tcf7l1a mutants have a much-reduced eye field compared to wildtype embryos.
source: Despite the much-reduced eye field in tcf7l1a mutants, these fish develop normal eyes revealing a striking ability of the eye to recover from a severe early phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 2 showing that the eye field volume in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants is reduced to 54.7% of wildtype size at 10hpf, and by RT-qPCR showing rx3 expression reduced to 26% of wildtype levels.

claim: tcf7l1a mutants develop normal eyes despite the reduced eye field.
source: Despite the much-reduced eye field in tcf7l1a mutants, these fish develop normal eyes revealing a striking ability of the eye to recover from a severe early phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos from six pairings developed eyes only slightly reduced in size compared to wildtype embryos (Figure 1A,B), and by optokinetic response data showing no significant differences between Ztcf7l1a-/- and wildtype larvae (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: The robustness of eye development in tcf7l1a mutants is not mediated through genetic compensation at neural plate stage.
source: This robustness is not mediated through genetic compensation at neural plate stage; instead, the smaller optic vesicle of tcf7l1a mutants shows delayed neurogenesis and continues to grow until it achieves approximately normal size.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data showing that expression levels of lef/tcf genes did not increase in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos at 10hpf (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1A).

claim: The smaller optic vesicle of tcf7l1a mutants shows delayed neurogenesis.
source: This robustness is not mediated through genetic compensation at neural plate stage; instead, the smaller optic vesicle of tcf7l1a mutants shows delayed neurogenesis and continues to grow until it achieves approximately normal size.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that atoh7 expression progression is delayed by about 8-12 hours in Ztcf7l1a-/- retinas compared to siblings (Figure 5A-J,Q, Supplementary file 1J).

claim: The developing eye is sensitised to the effects of additional mutations in the absence of Tcf7l1a function.
source: Although the developing eye is robust to the lack of Tcf7l1a function, it is sensitised to the effects of additional mutations.
evidence: This claim is supported by data from a forward genetic screen that identified mutations in hesx1, cct5 and gdf6a, which give synthetically enhanced eye specification or growth phenotypes when in combination with the tcf7l1a mutation (Figures 7-9).

claim: A forward genetic screen identified mutations in hesx1, cct5 and gdf6a that give synthetically enhanced eye phenotypes when combined with the tcf7l1a mutation.
source: In support of this, a forward genetic screen identified mutations in hesx1, cct5 and gdf6a, which give synthetically enhanced eye specification or growth phenotypes when in combination with the tcf7l1a mutation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that double mutants for hesx1/tcf7l1a are eyeless (Figure 7J,K), cct5/tcf7l1a mutants show compromised eye growth (Figure 8), and gdf6a/tcf7l1a mutants show reduced eye field and compromised size recovery (Figure 9).

claim: Enhanced Wnt/β-Catenin activity leads to embryos with small or no eyes.
source: Enhanced Wnt/β-Catenin activity leads to embryos with small or no eyes (Cavodeassi et al., 2005; Kim et al., 2000; Heisenberg et al., 2001; Houart et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Cavodeassi et al., 2005; Kim et al., 2000; Heisenberg et al., 2001; Houart et al., 2002).

claim: Decreasing activity of Wnt/β-Catenin signalling generates embryos with bigger forebrain and eyes.
source: In contrast, decreasing activity of Wnt/β-Catenin signalling generates embryos with bigger forebrain and eyes (Cavodeassi et al., 2005; Glinka et al., 1998; Lekven et al., 2001; Houart et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Cavodeassi et al., 2005; Glinka et al., 1998; Lekven et al., 2001; Houart et al., 2002).

claim: Maternal-zygotic tcf7l1a mutant zebrafish have been previously described as lacking eyes.
source: Maternal-zygotic tcf7l1a mutant zebrafish have been previously described as lacking eyes (Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kim et al., 2000).

claim: The expression of the eyeless phenotype in tcf7l1a mutants is dependent on the genetic background.
source: In this study, we show that expression of this phenotype is dependent on the genetic background.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that after three generations of outcrossing to EKW or AB fish, all MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos developed eyes only slightly reduced in size (Figure 1A,B), whereas in the original facility, MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos showed a variable eye phenotype.

claim: tcf7l1a mutants can develop functional eyes and are viable.
source: We find that tcf7l1a mutants can develop functional eyes and are viable, and that this is not due to compensatory upregulation of other lef/tcf genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos develop eyes (Figure 1A,B), show normal optokinetic responses (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), and that adult tcf7l1a mutants are viable.

claim: The eye field in tcf7l1a mutants is only half the size of the eye field of wildtype embryos.
source: Despite the presence of functional eyes, the eye field in tcf7l1a mutants is only half the size of the eye field of wildtype embryos, indicating an early requirement for tcf7l1a during eye field specification.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that the eye field volume in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants is reduced to 54.7% of wildtype size at 10hpf (Figure 2C,J-M, Supplementary file 1C).

claim: Tcf7l1a is required during eye field specification.
source: Despite the presence of functional eyes, the eye field in tcf7l1a mutants is only half the size of the eye field of wildtype embryos, indicating an early requirement for tcf7l1a during eye field specification.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing reduced eye field size in tcf7l1a mutants at 10hpf (Figure 2), and by cell transplantation experiments showing cell-autonomous requirement for Tcf7l1a in rx3 expression (Figure 3).

claim: tcf7l1a mutant eyes recover their size by delaying neurogenesis and prolonging growth in comparison to wildtype eyes.
source: Subsequent to compromised eye field specification, tcf7l1a mutant eyes recover their size by delaying neurogenesis and prolonging growth in comparison to wildtype eyes.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing delayed atoh7 expression progression in tcf7l1a mutants (Figure 5), increased proportion of proliferating cells (Figure 6C), and growth kinetics showing temporal offset between wildtype and mutant eyes (Figure 4A).

claim: The compensatory ability of the developing eye was observed when cells were removed from wild-type optic vesicles.
source: This compensatory ability of the developing eye was also observed when cells were removed from wild-type optic vesicles.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that wildtype eyes from which cells were removed at 12hpf recovered to approximately normal size by 4dpf (Figure 4M-O, Figure 4—figure supplement 4).

claim: The loss of Tcf7l1a does not trigger genetic compensation or signalling pathway changes that restore eye field specification.
source: Altogether, our study suggests that the loss of Tcf7l1a does not trigger any genetic compensation or signalling pathway changes that restore eye field specification; instead, the developing optic vesicle shows a remarkable ability to subsequently modulate its development to compensate for the early, severe loss of eye field progenitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data showing no compensatory upregulation of lef/tcf genes (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1A), and by the observation that the eye field remains reduced in tcf7l1a mutants at 10hpf.

claim: The developing optic vesicle shows a remarkable ability to modulate its development to compensate for the early, severe loss of eye field progenitors.
source: Altogether, our study suggests that the loss of Tcf7l1a does not trigger any genetic compensation or signalling pathway changes that restore eye field specification; instead, the developing optic vesicle shows a remarkable ability to subsequently modulate its development to compensate for the early, severe loss of eye field progenitors.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that despite a much-reduced eye field, tcf7l1a mutant eyes recover to approximately normal size through delayed neurogenesis and prolonged growth (Figures 4-6).

claim: The penetrance and expressivity of eye phenotypes appears to be dependent on complex genetic and environmental interactions.
source: The penetrance and expressivity of eye phenotypes appears to be dependent on complex genetic and environmental interactions (Gestri et al., 2009; Kaukonen et al., 2018; Prokudin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Gestri et al., 2009; Kaukonen et al., 2018; Prokudin et al., 2014).

claim: tcf7l1a mutant eyes are sensitised to the effects of additional mutations.
source: Thus, we speculated that tcf7l1a mutant eyes may be sensitised to the effects of additional mutations. Here, we show this is indeed the case and describe the isolation of three mutations from a recessive synthetic modifier screen in tcf7l1a homozygous mutant zebrafish that lead to enhanced/novel eye phenotypes when in combination with loss of tcf7l1a function.
evidence: This claim is supported by data from a forward genetic screen identifying mutations in hesx1, cct5 and gdf6a that give synthetically enhanced eye phenotypes when combined with the tcf7l1a mutation (Figures 7-9).

claim: Zebrafish eye development is robust to the effects of a mutation in tcf7l1a due to compensatory growth mechanisms that may link eye size and neurogenesis.
source: In summary, our work shows that zebrafish eye development is robust to the effects of a mutation in tcf7l1a due to compensatory growth mechanisms that may link eye size and neurogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing delayed neurogenesis in tcf7l1a mutants (Figure 5), increased proliferation (Figure 6), and premature neurogenesis in experimentally enlarged eyes (Figure 5M,N).

claim: All MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos from six pairings of Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant fish developed eyes only slightly reduced in size compared to eyes of wildtype embryos.
source: All MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos coming from six pairings of Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant fish developed eyes only slightly reduced in size compared to eyes of wildtype embryos of the same EKW or AB strain (100%, n > 100; Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from six pairings showing 100% of MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos developed eyes, and by images in Figure 1A,B showing eye morphology.

claim: The tcf7l1am881 mutation creates a splice acceptor site in intron 7, which leads to a seven nucleotide insertion in tcf7l1a mRNA.
source: The tcf7l1am881 mutation creates a splice acceptor site in intron 7, which leads to a seven nucleotide insertion in tcf7l1a mRNA that gives rise to a truncated protein due to a premature termination codon (Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to a previous study (Kim et al., 2000) and by RT-PCR data showing the seven nucleotide insertion in mutant mRNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Only mutant mRNA containing the seven nucleotide insertion was observed in tcf7l1a-/- mutants.
source: The chromatogram sequence of the RT-PCR product amplifying exons 7 and 8 in wildtype, mutant and heterozygous embryos showed that only wildtype tcf7l1a mRNA was detected in wildtype embryos and only mutant mRNA containing the seven nucleotide insertion was observed in mutants, while heterozygous embryos produced both wildtype and mutant mRNAs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-PCR chromatogram data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The mutant splice site is the only one used in tcf7l1a-/- embryos.
source: This suggests that the mutant splice site is the only one used in tcf7l1a-/- embryos.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the RT-PCR data showing only mutant mRNA in tcf7l1a-/- embryos (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).

claim: Overexpression of wildtype tcf7l1a mRNA rescued eye formation in embryos in which both tcf7l1a and tcf7l1b are knocked down.
source: In addition, while overexpression of wildtype tcf7l1a mRNA rescued eye formation in embryos in which both tcf7l1a and tcf7l1b are knocked down, tcf7l1am881 mutant mRNA did not, confirming that protein arising from the tcf7l1am881 allele is not functional (not shown; Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data (not shown in manuscript) and a citation to Kim et al., 2000.

claim: Protein arising from the tcf7l1am881 allele is not functional.
source: In addition, while overexpression of wildtype tcf7l1a mRNA rescued eye formation in embryos in which both tcf7l1a and tcf7l1b are knocked down, tcf7l1am881 mutant mRNA did not, confirming that protein arising from the tcf7l1am881 allele is not functional (not shown; Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that tcf7l1am881 mutant mRNA did not rescue eye formation, and by citation to Kim et al., 2000.

claim: The m881 allele is a null mutation.
source: These observations suggest that the m881 allele is indeed a null mutation and that tcf7l1a is not essential for eye formation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from multiple lines of evidence: only mutant mRNA is produced, the mutant protein is non-functional, and the mutation shows complete molecular penetrance.

claim: tcf7l1a is not essential for eye formation.
source: These observations suggest that the m881 allele is indeed a null mutation and that tcf7l1a is not essential for eye formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos develop functional eyes (Figures 1, 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: Antisense morpholino knockdown of tcf7l1a (mo1tcf7l1a) leads to eyeless embryos.
source: Supporting a requirement for tcf7l1a to form eyes, antisense morpholino knockdown of tcf7l1a (mo1tcf7l1a) leads to eyeless embryos (Dorsky et al., 2003) comparable to the originally described headless MZtcf7l1a-/- mutant phenotype (Kim et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Dorsky et al., 2003; Kim et al., 2000).

claim: The mo1tcf7l1a morpholino shows considerable sequence homology to the translation start ATG region of other tcf gene family members (56–76%).
source: However, the target site for the morpholino used in that study shows considerable sequence homology to the translation start ATG region of other tcf gene family members (56–76%; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The mo1tcf7l1a phenotype may be due to the morpholino knocking down expression of other tcf genes.
source: This suggests that the mo1tcf7l1a phenotype may be due to the morpholino knocking down expression of other tcf genes, as has been described for other morpholinos targeting paralogous genes (Kamachi et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the sequence homology data and supported by citation to Kamachi et al., 2008.

claim: Injection of mo2tcf7l1a morpholino did not lead to an eyeless phenotype.
source: Indeed, injection of a different tcf7l1a morpholino (mo2tcf7l1a) with low homology to other tcf genes (36–45%, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B) did not lead to an eyeless phenotype (0.4 pMol/embryo, 100%, n > 100; Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing no eyeless phenotype in 100% of embryos (n > 100) injected with mo2tcf7l1a, and by images in Figure 1C,D.

claim: tcf7l1b morpholino injection on its own showed no overt phenotype.
source: tcf7l1b morpholino injection on its own showed no overt phenotype (Dorsky et al., 2003) but co-injection of mo2tcf7l1a and motcf7l1b gave rise to eyeless embryos (each at 0.2 pMol/embryo, 78.26%, n = 92, over three experiments; Figure 1E and see Dorsky et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dorsky et al., 2003.

claim: Co-injection of mo2tcf7l1a and motcf7l1b gave rise to eyeless embryos (78.26%, n = 92).
source: tcf7l1b morpholino injection on its own showed no overt phenotype (Dorsky et al., 2003) but co-injection of mo2tcf7l1a and motcf7l1b gave rise to eyeless embryos (each at 0.2 pMol/embryo, 78.26%, n = 92, over three experiments; Figure 1E and see Dorsky et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing 78.26% eyeless embryos (n = 92) after co-injection, and by image in Figure 1E.

claim: Even though mo2tcf7l1a injection alone resulted in no phenotype, the morpholino does knockdown tcf7l1a.
source: This suggests that even though mo2tcf7l1a injection alone resulted in no phenotype, the morpholino does knockdown tcf7l1a.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that co-injection of mo2tcf7l1a and motcf7l1b produces an eyeless phenotype, suggesting that mo2tcf7l1a is functional.

claim: Lack of maternal and zygotic tcf7l1a function alone does not lead to loss of eyes in all genetic backgrounds.
source: Together, these results suggest that even though tcf7l1a-/- is a fully penetrant null mutation, lack of maternal and zygotic tcf7l1a function alone does not lead to loss of eyes in all genetic backgrounds.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing that MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos develop eyes in EKW and AB backgrounds, but the original report showed eyeless phenotype in a different background.

claim: Ztcf7l1a-/- and MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos develop eyes, whereas embryos lacking both Ztcf7l1a and Ztcf7l1b do not.
source: Ztcf7l1a-/- and MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos develop eyes, whereas embryos lacking both Ztcf7l1a and Ztcf7l1b do not (Dorsky et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dorsky et al., 2003 and by data showing that co-injection of mo2tcf7l1a and motcf7l1b produces eyeless embryos (Figure 1E).

claim: Expression levels of lef/tcf genes did not increase in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos.
source: Expression levels of lef/tcf genes did not increase in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos suggesting that there is no compensatory upregulation (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: tcf7l1a undergoes nonsense-mediated decay in mutants resulting in reduced expression levels.
source: As previously shown, tcf7l1a undergoes nonsense-mediated decay in mutants resulting in reduced expression levels (Kim et al., 2000; Figure 2A; Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Kim et al., 2000 and by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: lef1 and tcf7 levels did not change significantly in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: lef1 and tcf7 levels did not change significantly in mutants and tcf7l1b (tcf3b) and tcf7l2 (tcf4) expression was actually reduced to 63 ± 6% and 62 ± 8% respectively of wildtype levels (Figure 2A; Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: tcf7l1b expression was reduced to 63 ± 6% of wildtype levels in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: lef1 and tcf7 levels did not change significantly in mutants and tcf7l1b (tcf3b) and tcf7l2 (tcf4) expression was actually reduced to 63 ± 6% and 62 ± 8% respectively of wildtype levels (Figure 2A; Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: tcf7l2 expression was reduced to 62 ± 8% of wildtype levels in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: lef1 and tcf7 levels did not change significantly in mutants and tcf7l1b (tcf3b) and tcf7l2 (tcf4) expression was actually reduced to 63 ± 6% and 62 ± 8% respectively of wildtype levels (Figure 2A; Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: otx1b expression was reduced to 81 ± 11% of wildtype levels in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: The otx1b and otx2 genes, which are expressed in the anterior neural plate, also showed slightly reduced expression (otx1b, reduced to 81 ± 11% and otx2, 79 ± 10%) suggesting that the anterior neural plate may be slightly reduced in size in tcf7l1a mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data mentioned in the text and shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: otx2 expression was reduced to 79 ± 10% of wildtype levels in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: The otx1b and otx2 genes, which are expressed in the anterior neural plate, also showed slightly reduced expression (otx1b, reduced to 81 ± 11% and otx2, 79 ± 10%) suggesting that the anterior neural plate may be slightly reduced in size in tcf7l1a mutants.
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data mentioned in the text and shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: The anterior neural plate may be slightly reduced in size in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: The otx1b and otx2 genes, which are expressed in the anterior neural plate, also showed slightly reduced expression (otx1b, reduced to 81 ± 11% and otx2, 79 ± 10%) suggesting that the anterior neural plate may be slightly reduced in size in tcf7l1a mutants.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the reduced expression of otx1b and otx2 genes, and supported by data showing the forebrain domain is reduced to 76% of wildtype size (Figure 2B).

claim: A reduction in the size of the prospective forebrain of Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos may contribute to the reduced levels of expression of tcf7l1b, tcf7l2 and otx genes.
source: This indicates that a reduction in the size of the prospective forebrain of Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos may contribute to the reduced levels of expression of tcf7l1b, tcf7l2 and otx genes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that the forebrain domain is reduced in size and that genes expressed in this domain show reduced expression levels.

claim: RT-qPCR showed very reduced expression of eye field genes in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos.
source: More remarkable than the modest changes in tcf and otx gene expression was the finding that RT-qPCR showed very reduced expression of eye field genes in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos (Figure 2A; rx3 reduced to 26 ± 1%, p=0.0002 and six3b reduced to 44 ± 5%, p=0.0091 of wildtype levels).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: rx3 expression was reduced to 26 ± 1% of wildtype levels in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos.
source: More remarkable than the modest changes in tcf and otx gene expression was the finding that RT-qPCR showed very reduced expression of eye field genes in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos (Figure 2A; rx3 reduced to 26 ± 1%, p=0.0002 and six3b reduced to 44 ± 5%, p=0.0091 of wildtype levels).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: six3b expression was reduced to 44 ± 5% of wildtype levels in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos.
source: More remarkable than the modest changes in tcf and otx gene expression was the finding that RT-qPCR showed very reduced expression of eye field genes in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos (Figure 2A; rx3 reduced to 26 ± 1%, p=0.0002 and six3b reduced to 44 ± 5%, p=0.0091 of wildtype levels).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2A and Supplementary file 1A.

claim: rx3-/- mutant embryos lack eyes due to impaired specification/evagination of the optic vesicles.
source: Consequently, the presence of overtly normal looking eyes in both Ztcf7l1a-/- and MZtcf7l1a-/- embryos is surprising given that rx3-/- mutant embryos lack eyes due to impaired specification/evagination of the optic vesicles (Loosli et al., 2003; Stigloher et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Loosli et al., 2003; Stigloher et al., 2006).

claim: Expression of six3b and rx3 is reduced in the anterior neural plate in Ztcf7l1a-/- and tcf7l1a morphant embryos.
source: We confirmed that expression of six3b and rx3 is reduced in the anterior neural plate by in situ hybridisation in Ztcf7l1a-/- and tcf7l1a morphant embryos (100%,n > 40; Figure 2F–I; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B; similar changes seen in MZtcf7l1a-/- mutants, data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 2F-I and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The expression of six3b was reduced in the eye field but not in the prechordal plate of Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants.
source: The expression of six3b was reduced in the eye field but not in the prechordal plate of Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants, likely explaining why RT-qPCR showed a greater reduction in rx3 than six3b expression (Figure 2F–I; Supplementary file 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 2F-I.

claim: Analysis of eye field volume by fluorescent in situ hybridisation of rx3 revealed a reduction to 54.7% of wildtype size.
source: Analysis of eye field volume by fluorescent in situ hybridisation of rx3 revealed a reduction to 54.7% of wildtype size (n = 10, Figure 2C,J–M; Supplementary file 1C) and intensity of expression within the reduced eye field also appeared reduced (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric analysis data shown in Figure 2C and Supplementary file 1C, and by fluorescent in situ hybridisation images in Figure 2J-M.

claim: Intensity of rx3 expression within the reduced eye field appeared reduced in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: Analysis of eye field volume by fluorescent in situ hybridisation of rx3 revealed a reduction to 54.7% of wildtype size (n = 10, Figure 2C,J–M; Supplementary file 1C) and intensity of expression within the reduced eye field also appeared reduced (Figure 2H,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation images shown in Figure 2H,I.

claim: It is the caudal region of the eye field that is most affected in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants.
source: Further in situ hybridasation analysis suggests that it is the caudal region of the eye field that is most affected in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants.
evidence: This claim is inferred from in situ hybridisation data showing that emx3 expression rostral to the eye field is slightly broader but does not encroach into the reduced eye field, while barhl2 expression caudal to the eye field is expanded rostrally (Figure 2D,E; Figure 2—figure supplement 2).

claim: emx3 expression directly rostral to the eye field was slightly broader in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants than wildtypes but expression did not encroach into the reduced eye field.
source: emx3 expression directly rostral to the eye field was slightly broader in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants than wildtypes but expression did not encroach into the reduced eye field (Figure 2D,E; Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B, n = 5 each condition).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 2D,E and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Expression of the prospective diencephalic marker barhl2 caudal to the reduced eye field was expanded rostrally at 10hpf in tcf7l1a mutants.
source: Conversely, expression of the prospective diencephalic marker barhl2 caudal to the reduced eye field was expanded rostrally at 10hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C,D n = 5 each condition) and even more evidently at 9hpf (Figure 2—figure supplement 2E,F, 13/13 Ztcf7l1a-/-).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-F.

claim: These observations suggest a caudalisation of the anterior neural plate in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants leading to reduced eye field specification.
source: These observations suggest a caudalisation of the anterior neural plate in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants leading to reduced eye field specification consistent with phenotypes observed in conditions in which Wnt pathway repression is reduced (Heisenberg et al., 2001; van de Water et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the in situ hybridisation data showing rostral expansion of barhl2 and is supported by citations to previous studies (Heisenberg et al., 2001; van de Water et al., 2001).

claim: RNAseq analysis of wildtype, Ztcf7l1a-/- and Ztcf7l1a-/-/Ztcf7l1b+/- embryos at 8.5hpf confirmed and extended RT-qPCR and in situ hybridisation analyses.
source: RNAseq analysis of wildtype, Ztcf7l1a-/- and Ztcf7l1a-/-/Ztcf7l1b+/- embryos at 8.5hpf (80–90% epiboly stage), when the eye field is first specified confirmed and extended RT-qPCR and in situ hybridisation analyses (Supplementary file 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in Supplementary file 1D.

claim: In Ztcf7l1a-/-, hesx1, rx3, tcf7l1a, and fezf2 which are expressed in the prospective forebrain/eyefield were downregulated.
source: In Ztcf7l1a-/-, hesx1 (Kazanskaya et al., 1997), rx3, tcf7l1a, and fezf2 (Sun et al., 2006) which are expressed in the prospective forebrain/eyefield were downregulated, whereas her5 and irx1b which are expressed more caudally in the neural plate (Müller et al., 1996, Wang et al., 2001b) were upregulated consistent with mild caudalisation of the neural plate.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data (Supplementary file 1D) and citations to previous studies (Kazanskaya et al., 1997; Sun et al., 2006; Müller et al., 1996; Wang et al., 2001b).

claim: her5 and irx1b which are expressed more caudally in the neural plate were upregulated in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants.
source: In Ztcf7l1a-/-, hesx1 (Kazanskaya et al., 1997), rx3, tcf7l1a, and fezf2 (Sun et al., 2006) which are expressed in the prospective forebrain/eyefield were downregulated, whereas her5 and irx1b which are expressed more caudally in the neural plate (Müller et al., 1996, Wang et al., 2001b) were upregulated consistent with mild caudalisation of the neural plate.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data (Supplementary file 1D) and citations to previous studies (Müller et al., 1996; Wang et al., 2001b).

claim: In Ztcf7l1a-/-/tcf7l1b+/- embryos, which do not form eyes, the expression of tcf7l1b was enhanced by about 40%.
source: Additionally, in Ztcf7l1a-/-/tcf7l1b+/- embryos, which to not form eyes, the expression of tcf7l1b was enhanced by about 40%, suggesting transcriptional compensation but evidently this was not sufficient to rescue eye formation.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAseq data (Supplementary file 1D).

claim: The enhanced expression of tcf7l1b in Ztcf7l1a-/-/tcf7l1b+/- embryos suggests transcriptional compensation but this was not sufficient to rescue eye formation.
source: Additionally, in Ztcf7l1a-/-/tcf7l1b+/- embryos, which to not form eyes, the expression of tcf7l1b was enhanced by about 40%, suggesting transcriptional compensation but evidently this was not sufficient to rescue eye formation.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that tcf7l1b expression is enhanced but eyes still do not form in Ztcf7l1a-/-/tcf7l1b+/- embryos.

claim: Optic vesicles appear to evaginate normally in tcf7l1a-/- mutants despite the small size of eye field.
source: Despite the small size of eye field in tcf7l1a-/- mutants, optic vesicles appear to evaginate normally.
evidence: This claim is supported by time lapse analysis data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3 and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Time lapse analysis showed that optic vesicle morphogenesis in Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos proceeded as in heterozygous sibling embryos.
source: Time lapse analysis of optic vesicle evagination using the Tg(rx3:GFP)zf460Tg transgene to visualise eye field cells (Brown et al., 2010) showed that optic vesicle morphogenesis in Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos proceeded as in heterozygous sibling embryos (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B; tcf7l1a+/-, n = 6 and Ztcf7l1a-/- n = 6; Video 1 and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by time lapse imaging data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A,B and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: Transplants of wildtype cells to MZtcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos led to the recovery of rx3 expression exclusively restricted to the wildtype GFP+ cell clones.
source: Transplants of wildtype cells to MZtcf7l1a-/- mutant embryos led to the recovery of rx3 expression exclusively restricted to the wildtype GFP+ cell clones (13/13 transplants, Figure 3A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell transplantation data shown in Figure 3A-C (13/13 transplants).

claim: The border of the GFP+ wildtype clones showed less rx3 expression, suggesting that cells at the edge of the graft are subject to cell non-autonomous signalling effects from cells surrounding the clone.
source: However, the border of the GFP+ wildtype clones showed less rx3 expression, suggesting that cells at the edge of the graft are subject to cell non-autonomous signalling effects from cells surrounding the clone.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that rx3 expression is reduced at the border of wildtype cell clones in mutant hosts (Figure 3A-C).

claim: MZtcf7l1a-/- mutant GFP+ cells expressed much lower levels of rx3 than wildtype neighbours when positioned in the eye field of wildtype embryos.
source: Conversely, MZtcf7l1a-/- mutant GFP+ cells expressed much lower levels of rx3 than wildtype neighbours when positioned in the eye field of wildtype embryos (9/9 transplants, Figure 3D–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell transplantation data shown in Figure 3D-F (9/9 transplants).

claim: The reduction in rx3 expression was limited to the MZtcf7l1a-/- GFP+ mutant cells.
source: The reduction in rx3 expression was limited to the MZtcf7l1a-/- GFP+ mutant cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell transplantation data shown in Figure 3D-F.

claim: Overexpression of the Wnt inhibitor Dkk1 expanded the anterior neural plate in both wildtype and tcf7l1a mutants.
source: Consistent with a cell autonomous role for Tcf7l1a in eye formation, overexpression of the Wnt inhibitor Dkk1 (Hashimoto et al., 2000) expanded the anterior neural plate in both wildtype and tcf7l1a mutants, but rx3 expression and eye field size remained much smaller in the enlarged anterior plate of tcf7l1a mutants (Figure 3G–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 3G-J and citation to Hashimoto et al., 2000.

claim: rx3 expression and eye field size remained much smaller in the enlarged anterior plate of tcf7l1a mutants after Dkk1 overexpression.
source: Consistent with a cell autonomous role for Tcf7l1a in eye formation, overexpression of the Wnt inhibitor Dkk1 (Hashimoto et al., 2000) expanded the anterior neural plate in both wildtype and tcf7l1a mutants, but rx3 expression and eye field size remained much smaller in the enlarged anterior plate of tcf7l1a mutants (Figure 3G–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 3G-J.

claim: Tcf7l1a has a cell-autonomous role in promoting eye field specification.
source: All together, these results support a cell-autonomous role for Tcf7l1a in promoting eye field specification.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell transplantation experiments (Figure 3A-F) and Dkk1 overexpression experiments (Figure 3G-J).

claim: Eyes in Ztcf7l1a-/- fry and adults seem indistinguishable from those in wildtype siblings.
source: Despite a much-reduced eye field, eyes in Ztcf7l1a-/- fry and adults seem indistinguishable from those in wildtype siblings.
evidence: This claim is supported by visual observation and optokinetic response data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: Optokinetic responses of Ztcf7l1a-/- and wildtype 5dpf larvae showed no significant differences at any of the four tested spatial frequencies.
source: Indeed, optokinetic responses of Ztcf7l1a-/- and wildtype 5dpf larvae showed no significant differences at any of the four tested spatial frequencies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1E), suggesting that by this stage, Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes are functional and have visual acuity comparable to that of wildtype siblings.
evidence: This claim is supported by optokinetic response data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1E.

claim: By 5dpf, Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes are functional and have visual acuity comparable to that of wildtype siblings.
source: Indeed, optokinetic responses of Ztcf7l1a-/- and wildtype 5dpf larvae showed no significant differences at any of the four tested spatial frequencies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1E), suggesting that by this stage, Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes are functional and have visual acuity comparable to that of wildtype siblings.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the optokinetic response data showing no significant differences between wildtype and mutant larvae (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).

claim: At 24hpf, eye volume in tcf7l1a mutants was about 57% of the estimated volume of wildtype eyes at the same stage.
source: At 24hpf, eye volume in mutants was about 57% of the estimated volume of wildtype eyes at the same stage (Figure 4A,C,H; Supplementary file 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 4A and Supplementary file 1F.

claim: By 48hpf mutant eyes were about 85% of the size of eyes in wildtype/heterozygous siblings.
source: However, by 48hpf mutant eyes were about 85% of the size of eyes in wildtype/heterozygous siblings (Figure 4A,G,L; Supplementary file 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 4A and Supplementary file 1F.

claim: Ztcf7l1a-/- eye size did not further recover beyond 48hpf and up to 5dpf.
source: Ztcf7l1a-/- eye size did not further recover beyond this time point and up to 5dpf (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B showing the ratio of Ztcf7l1a-/- to wildtype eye volume plateaus after 48hpf.

claim: Eye growth in both wildtypes and Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants showed similar growth kinetics.
source: Eye growth in both wildtypes and Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants showed similar growth kinetics (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth kinetics data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes follow a comparable developmental time-course as wildtype eyes in the early growth phase between 24 and 36hpf but with about 8 hr delay.
source: This suggests that even though Ztcf7l1a-/-eyes are smaller, they follow a comparable developmental time-course as wildtype eyes in the early growth phase between 24 and 36hpf but with about 8 hr delay (for instance, a 32hpf Ztcf7l1a-/- eye is about the same size as a wild-type 24hpf eye).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the growth kinetics data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The temporal shift in eye growth in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants is not explained by an overall developmental delay.
source: The temporal shift in eye growth in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants is not explained by an overall developmental delay as the position of the posterior lateral line primordium (pLLP) was similar to wildtype at all stages tested (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing similar pLLP position in wildtype and mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 1G).

claim: Volumes of eye cells in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants and siblings were not significantly different at 24 or 36hpf.
source: Volumes of eye cells in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants and siblings were not significantly different at 24 or 36hpf and consequently cell size changes likely play no role in eye size compensation in Ztcf7l1a mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell volume quantification data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Supplementary file 1H.

claim: Cell size changes likely play no role in eye size compensation in Ztcf7l1a mutants.
source: Volumes of eye cells in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants and siblings were not significantly different at 24 or 36hpf and consequently cell size changes likely play no role in eye size compensation in Ztcf7l1a mutants (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Supplementary file 1H).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that cell volumes are not significantly different between wildtype and mutants.

claim: At 36hpf, there was still a clear size difference between the experimental and control eyes after partial ablation of the optic vesicle.
source: At 36hpf, there was still a clear size difference between the experimental and control eyes (Figure 4N, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4N and Figure 4—figure supplement 4, and quantification data in Supplementary file 1I.

claim: By 4dpf there was little or no size difference between control and experimental eyes after partial ablation of the optic vesicle.
source: However, by 4dpf we observed little or no size difference between control and experimental eyes (three independent experiments, n=20/20, Figure 4O, Figure 4—figure supplement 4, Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 4O and Figure 4—figure supplement 4, and quantification data in Supplementary file 1I (n=20/20).

claim: Three eyes from partially ablated optic vesicles which were ~90% the size of their control contralateral eyes at 30hpf, recovered to 100% by 3dpf.
source: Three eyes from partially ablated optic vesicles which were ~90% the size of their control contralateral eyes at 30hpf, recovered to 100% by 3dpf (Figure 4—figure supplement 4K, Supplementary file 1I) and five eyes which were between ~65 and~75% of control size at 30hpf recovered to 90% by 3dpf with little or no further recovery by 4dpf (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A–I,K, Supplementary file 1I).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4K and Supplementary file 1I.

claim: The forming eye can effectively recover from either genetic or physical reduction in the size of the eye field/evaginating optic vesicle.
source: Consequently, the forming eye can effectively recover from either genetic or physical reduction in the size of the eye field/evaginating optic vesicle.
evidence: This claim is inferred from data showing size recovery in both tcf7l1a mutants and after physical ablation of optic vesicle cells.

claim: Retinal neurogenesis might be delayed in Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes to extend the period of proliferative growth prior to retinal precursors undergoing neurogenic divisions.
source: The observation that wildtype and Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant eyes display similar, but temporally offset, growth kinetics led us to speculate that that retinal neurogenesis might be delayed in Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes to extend the period of proliferative growth prior to retinal precursors undergoing neurogenic divisions.
evidence: This claim is a speculation based on the observation of similar but temporally offset growth kinetics.

claim: In the zebrafish eye, neurogenesis can be visualised by tracking expression of atoh7 starting in the ventronasal retina at ~28 hpf and spreading clockwise across the central retina until it reaches the ventrotemporal side.
source: In the zebrafish eye, neurogenesis can be visualised by tracking expression of atoh7 (ath5) in retinal neurons starting in the ventronasal retina at ~28 hpf and spreading clockwise across the central retina until it reaches the ventrotemporal side (Masai et al., 2000; Hu and Easter, 1999; Figure 5A–E,Q, Supplementary file 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Masai et al., 2000; Hu and Easter, 1999) and by data shown in Figure 5A-E,Q and Supplementary file 1J.

claim: atoh7 was induced at a similar time in Ztcf7l1a-/- as in wildtype eyes.
source: Although atoh7 was induced at a similar time in Ztcf7l1a-/- as in wildtype eyes, the subsequent progression of expression was delayed (Figure 5F–J,Q; Supplementary file 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by atoh7 expression data shown in Figure 5F-J,Q and Supplementary file 1J.

claim: The subsequent progression of atoh7 expression was delayed in Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes.
source: Although atoh7 was induced at a similar time in Ztcf7l1a-/- as in wildtype eyes, the subsequent progression of expression was delayed (Figure 5F–J,Q; Supplementary file 1J).
evidence: This claim is supported by atoh7 expression data shown in Figure 5F-J,Q and Supplementary file 1J.

claim: Between 36 and 40hpf, Ztcf7l1a-/- retinas expressed atoh7 exclusively in the nasal half of the retina.
source: Indeed, between 36 and 40hpf, Ztcf7l1a-/- retinas expressed atoh7 exclusively in the nasal half of the retina (Figure 5H,Q), a phenotype we did not see at any stage in sibling embryo eyes.
evidence: This claim is supported by atoh7 expression data shown in Figure 5H,Q.

claim: Progression of atoh7 expression and neurogenesis is delayed by about 8–12 hr in Ztcf7l1a-/- retinas compared to siblings.
source: These data indicate that progression of atoh7 expression and neurogenesis is delayed by about 8–12 hr in Ztcf7l1a-/- retinas compared to siblings, a timeframe comparable to the delays seen in optic vesicle growth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the atoh7 expression data shown in Figure 5 and Supplementary file 1J.

claim: Eye vesicle ablated wildtype retinas showed delayed neurogenesis compared to control non-ablated contralateral eyes at 36hpf.
source: In line with our results in Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos, eye vesicle ablated wildtype retinas also showed delayed neurogenesis compared to control non-ablated contralateral eyes at 36hpf (Figure 5K,L; 6/6 ablated eyes, two independent experiments).
evidence: This claim is supported by atoh7 expression data shown in Figure 5K,L (6/6 ablated eyes).

claim: Retinal precursors in Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes remain proliferative at stages when precursors in wildtype eyes are already producing neurons.
source: Our results suggest that retinal precursors in Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes remain proliferative at stages when precursors in wildtype eyes are already producing neurons.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the delayed neurogenesis data (Figure 5) and increased proliferation data (Figure 6).

claim: Heatshocking tg(hsp70:dkk1-GFP)w32 transgenic embryos at 6hpf led to eyes ~ 34% bigger than control heat-shocked embryos by 28hpf.
source: Heatshocking tg(hsp70:dkk1-GFP)w32 transgenic embryos at 6hpf led to eyes ~ 34% bigger than control heat-shocked embryos by 28hpf (Figure 5M,N,R, n = 12; Supplementary file 1K).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye size quantification data shown in Figure 5M,N,R and Supplementary file 1K.

claim: After 36hpf, wildtype eyes gradually caught up in size as growth slowed in eyes in dkk1-overexpressed embryos.
source: After 36hpf, wildtype eyes gradually caught up in size as growth slowed in eyes in dkk1-overexpressed embryos (Figure 5R; Supplementary file 1K).
evidence: This claim is supported by growth kinetics data shown in Figure 5R and Supplementary file 1K.

claim: Neurogenesis was prematurely triggered by 28hpf in the eyes of dkk1 overexpressing embryos.
source: Neurogenesis was prematurely triggered by 28hpf in the eyes of dkk1 overexpressing embryos, with many more cells expressing atoh7 compared to eyes in heat-shocked control embryos (Figure 5M,N, n = 7 out of 9 embryos).
evidence: This claim is supported by atoh7 expression data shown in Figure 5M,N (n = 7 out of 9 embryos).

claim: The premature neurogenesis in dkk1 overexpressing embryos is unlikely to be due to a direct effect of dkk1 overexpression on neurogenesis.
source: This result is unlikely to be due to a direct effect of dkk1 overexpression on neurogenesis as premature neurogenesis was not triggered in tg(hsp70:dkk1-GFP)w32 retinas heat-shocked at 24hpf (Figure 5O,P, n = 10, 100%).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that heat shock at 24hpf does not trigger premature neurogenesis (Figure 5O,P).

claim: The results support a link between eye size and the onset of neurogenesis and the size self-regulating ability of the forming eye.
source: These results further support a link between eye size and the onset of neurogenesis and the size self-regulating ability of the forming eye.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observations that larger eyes show premature neurogenesis and smaller eyes show delayed neurogenesis.

claim: The proportion of PH3-positive cells standardised to the total number of cells in confocal sections at 36hpf was about 20% higher in Ztcf7l1a mutants than wildtypes.
source: The proportion of PH3-positive (PH3+) cells standardised to the total number of cells in confocal sections at 36hpf was about 20% higher in Ztcf7l1a mutants than wildtypes (Figure 6A,B,C, Supplementary file 1L, wildtype, n = 7; Ztcf7l1a-/-, n = 8, p=0.021, unpaired t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by PH3 quantification data shown in Figure 6A,B,C and Supplementary file 1L.

claim: The proportion of PH3+ cells was similar between nasal and temporal retina and similar between wildtypes and Ztcf7l1a mutants.
source: The proportion of PH3+ cells was similar between nasal and temporal retina and similar between wildtypes and Ztcf7l1a mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Supplementary file 1L).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 1L.

claim: The percentage of PH3+ RPCs co-expressing atoh7:GAP-RFP was 3.6 times higher in wildtypes compared to tcf7l1a mutants.
source: Furthermore, the percentage of PH3+ RPCs co-expressing atoh7:GAP-RFP was 3.6 times higher in wildtypes compared to tcf7l1a mutants (Figure 6A,B,D, Supplementary file 1L, wildtype, 35.21 ± 3.5, n = 7, Ztcf7l1a-/-, 9.67 ± 1.58, n = 8, unpaired t-test p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6A,B,D and Supplementary file 1L.

claim: Wildtype nasal RPCs were about three times more likely to be atoh7:GAP-RFP positive than nasal RPCs in mutants.
source: Wildtype nasal RPCs were about three times more likely to be atoh7:GAP-RFP positive than nasal RPCs in mutants (Figure 6D, Supplementary file 1L, wildtype, 45.91 ± 3.71, n = 7, Ztcf7l1a-/-, 15.44 ± 2.25, n = 8, unpaired t-test p<0.0001), and PH3+ RPCs in the temporal retina of tcf7l1a mutants almost never showed atoh7:GAP-RFP co-expression (Figure 6D, Supplementary file 1L, wildtype, 20.97 ± 3.67, n = 7, Ztcf7l1a-/-, 0.48 ± 0.48, n = 8, unpaired t-test p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6D and Supplementary file 1L.

claim: PH3+ RPCs in the temporal retina of tcf7l1a mutants almost never showed atoh7:GAP-RFP co-expression.
source: Wildtype nasal RPCs were about three times more likely to be atoh7:GAP-RFP positive than nasal RPCs in mutants (Figure 6D, Supplementary file 1L, wildtype, 45.91 ± 3.71, n = 7, Ztcf7l1a-/-, 15.44 ± 2.25, n = 8, unpaired t-test p<0.0001), and PH3+ RPCs in the temporal retina of tcf7l1a mutants almost never showed atoh7:GAP-RFP co-expression (Figure 6D, Supplementary file 1L, wildtype, 20.97 ± 3.67, n = 7, Ztcf7l1a-/-, 0.48 ± 0.48, n = 8, unpaired t-test p<0.0001).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 6D and Supplementary file 1L.

claim: At a stage when many wildtype RPCs are undergoing neurogenic divisions, more RPCs in tcf7l1a mutants are still proliferating, likely contributing to compensatory growth of the mutant eye.
source: These results suggest that at a stage when many wildtype RPCs are undergoing neurogenic divisions, more RPCs in tcf7l1a mutants are still proliferating, likely contributing to compensatory growth of the mutant eye.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the PH3 and atoh7:GAP-RFP co-expression data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Eye development in tcf7l1a-/- mutants might be sensitised to showing the effects of additional mutations.
source: Although eye formation can recover in tcf7l1a-/- mutants despite a much smaller eye field, we speculated that eye development in these embryos might be sensitised to showing the effects of additional mutations.
evidence: This is a speculation that is subsequently tested through a forward genetic screen.

claim: Homozygous U910 mutants that are heterozygous for the tcf7l1a mutation have normal eyes.
source: tcf7l1a-/- embryos homozygous for the U910 mutation were eyeless (Figure 7B,C) whereas homozygous U910 mutants with one or no mutant tcf7l1a alleles showed no eye phenotype.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the statement that homozygous U910 mutants with one or no mutant tcf7l1a alleles showed no eye phenotype, and supported by image in Figure 7B.

claim: U910 was mapped to a 1.46 Mb interval between 41.36 Mb and 42.82 Mb on chromosome 11.
source: U910 was mapped by SSLP segregation analysis (Kelly et al., 2000) to a 1.46 Mb interval between 41.36 Mb (four recombinants/276meioses) and 42.82 Mb (two recombinants/276meioses) on chromosome 11 in GRCz10 assembly (Figure 6D, Supplementary file 1M).
evidence: This claim is supported by mapping data shown in Figure 7D and Supplementary file 1M, and citation to Kelly et al., 2000.

claim: hesx1 is within the mapped interval for U910.
source: Within this interval is hesx1, which morpholino knock-down experiments had previously suggested to genetically interact with tcf7l1a (Andoniadou et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by the mapping data and citation to Andoniadou et al., 2011.

claim: Morpholino knock-down experiments had previously suggested that hesx1 genetically interacts with tcf7l1a.
source: Within this interval is hesx1, which morpholino knock-down experiments had previously suggested to genetically interact with tcf7l1a (Andoniadou et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Andoniadou et al., 2011.

claim: Primers for hesx1 cDNA failed to amplify in U910/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyeless embryo cDNA samples.
source: Primers for hesx1 cDNA failed to amplify in U910/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyeless embryo cDNA samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: All U910/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyeless embryos had a ~ 2700 bp deletion that covers hesx1 exons 1 and 2.
source: Using a primer set that spans the hesx1 locus, we found that all U910/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyeless embryos had a ~ 2700 bp deletion that covers hesx1 exons 1 and 2 (hesx1Δex1/2; Figure 7—figure supplement 1); this was unexpected as deletions are not normally induced by ENU (see below).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Deletions are not normally induced by ENU.
source: Using a primer set that spans the hesx1 locus, we found that all U910/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyeless embryos had a ~ 2700 bp deletion that covers hesx1 exons 1 and 2 (hesx1Δex1/2; Figure 7—figure supplement 1); this was unexpected as deletions are not normally induced by ENU (see below).
evidence: This is established knowledge about ENU mutagenesis.

claim: There is a polyA stretch of approximately 80 nucleotides followed by a 33 AT microsatellite repeat on the 3' end of intron two in the hesx1 locus.
source: Sequencing of the hesx1 locus revealed that there is a polyA stretch of approximately 80 nucleotides followed by a 33 AT microsatellite repeat on the 3' end of intron two that may have generated a chromosomal instability that led to the deletion of exons 1 and 2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The polyA stretch and AT microsatellite repeat may have generated a chromosomal instability that led to the deletion of exons 1 and 2 in hesx1.
source: Sequencing of the hesx1 locus revealed that there is a polyA stretch of approximately 80 nucleotides followed by a 33 AT microsatellite repeat on the 3' end of intron two that may have generated a chromosomal instability that led to the deletion of exons 1 and 2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a speculation based on the sequence features observed.

claim: hesx1 mRNA was not detected by RT-PCR or in situ hybridisation in U910 homozygous embryos.
source: As a consequence of the deletion, hesx1 mRNA was not detected by RT-PCR or in situ hybridisation in U910 homozygous embryos (Figure 6E,H,I).
evidence: This claim is supported by RT-PCR and in situ hybridisation data shown in Figure 7E,H,I.

claim: Only U910-F2 embryos that were homozygous for both the tcf7l1a mutation and hesx1U910/U910 were eyeless.
source: We further confirmed that only U910-F2 embryos that were homozygous for both the tcf7l1a mutation and hesx1U910/U910 were eyeless (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: ENU usually generates point mutations.
source: As ENU usually generates point mutations, we speculated that the deletion in hesx1Δex1/2 was not caused by our mutagenesis but was already present in one or more fish used to generate the mutant lines.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ENU mutagenesis.

claim: The deletion in hesx1Δex1/2 was not caused by ENU mutagenesis but was already present in one or more fish used to generate the mutant lines.
source: As ENU usually generates point mutations, we speculated that the deletion in hesx1Δex1/2 was not caused by our mutagenesis but was already present in one or more fish used to generate the mutant lines. Indeed, we found the same deletion in wildtype fish not used in the mutagenesis project.
evidence: This claim is supported by the finding of the same deletion in wildtype fish not used in the mutagenesis project.

claim: The same hesx1 deletion was found in wildtype fish not used in the mutagenesis project.
source: As ENU usually generates point mutations, we speculated that the deletion in hesx1Δex1/2 was not caused by our mutagenesis but was already present in one or more fish used to generate the mutant lines. Indeed, we found the same deletion in wildtype fish not used in the mutagenesis project.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data mentioned in the text.

claim: Incrossing of hesx1Δex1/2/Δex1/2/tcf7l1a+/- adult fish led to embryos with a very small rudiment of eye pigment with no detectable lens.
source: Incrossing of hesx1Δex1/2/Δex1/2/tcf7l1a+/- adult fish led to embryos with a very small rudiment of eye pigment with no detectable lens (Figure 7J,K).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 7J,K.

claim: Genotyping of eyeless and sibling embryos confirmed that only double homozygosity for hesx1Δex1/2/Ztcf7l1a-/- led to the eyeless embryo phenotype.
source: Genotyping of eyeless and sibling embryos confirmed that only double homozygosity for hesx1Δex1/2/Ztcf7l1a-/- led to the eyeless embryo phenotype (Four independent experiments, n = 53, Supplementary file 1N).
evidence: This claim is supported by genotyping data from four independent experiments (n = 53, Supplementary file 1N).

claim: The interaction between hesx1 and tcf7l1a mutations illustrates how the developing eye can fully cope with loss of function of either gene alone but fails to form in absence of both gene activities.
source: The interaction between hesx1 and tcf7l1a mutations strikingly illustrates how the developing eye can fully cope with loss of function of either gene alone but fails to form in absence of both gene activities.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that single mutants have eyes but double mutants do not.

claim: U762 mutant eyes showed no significant size difference compared to wildtypes at 36hpf.
source: U762 mutant eyes showed no significant size difference compared to wildtypes at 36hpf (Figure 8A,C,K, Supplementary file 1O); neither did Ztcf7l1a-/- compared to double U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes (Figure 8B,D,K, Supplementary file 1O).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 8A,C,K and Supplementary file 1O.

claim: Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes showed no significant size difference compared to double U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes at 36hpf.
source: U762 mutant eyes showed no significant size difference compared to wildtypes at 36hpf (Figure 8A,C,K, Supplementary file 1O); neither did Ztcf7l1a-/- compared to double U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes (Figure 8B,D,K, Supplementary file 1O).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 8B,D,K and Supplementary file 1O.

claim: By 52hpf U762 mutants showed slightly reduced eye size.
source: However, by 52hpf U762 mutants showed slightly reduced eye size and this phenotype was considerably more severe in embryos additionally homozygous for the Ztcf7l1a mutation (Figure 8F–I,K, Supplementary file 1O).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 8F-I,K and Supplementary file 1O.

claim: The eye size reduction phenotype in U762 mutants was considerably more severe in embryos additionally homozygous for the Ztcf7l1a mutation at 52hpf.
source: However, by 52hpf U762 mutants showed slightly reduced eye size and this phenotype was considerably more severe in embryos additionally homozygous for the Ztcf7l1a mutation (Figure 8F–I,K, Supplementary file 1O).

claim: The U762 mutation was mapped to a 1.69 Mb interval between 15.50 Mb and 17.19 Mb on chromosome 24.
source: The U762 mutation was mapped by SSLP segregation analysis to a 1.69 Mb interval between 15.50 Mb and 17.19 Mb on chromosome 24 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A) and through sequencing candidate genes in this interval (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A; Supplementary file 1P), we identified a mutation in the splice donor of cct5 (chaperonin containing TCP-1 epsilon) intron 4 (GT >GC, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mapping data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A mutation was identified in the splice donor of cct5 intron 4 (GT >GC) in U762.
source: The U762 mutation was mapped by SSLP segregation analysis to a 1.69 Mb interval between 15.50 Mb and 17.19 Mb on chromosome 24 (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A) and through sequencing candidate genes in this interval (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A; Supplementary file 1P), we identified a mutation in the splice donor of cct5 (chaperonin containing TCP-1 epsilon) intron 4 (GT >GC, Figure 8—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The cct5 mutation leads to the usage of an alternative splice donor in the 3' most end of cct5 exon 4, which induces a two nucleotide deletion in the mRNA.
source: The mutation leads to the usage of an alternative splice donor in the 3' most end of cct5 exon 4, which induces a two nucleotide deletion in the mRNA (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The two nucleotide deletion in cct5 mRNA changes the reading frame of the protein after amino acid 176, encoding a 29aa nonsense stretch followed by a stop codon.
source: This deletion changes the reading frame of the protein after amino acid 176, encoding a 29aa nonsense stretch followed by a stop codon (Figure 8—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by sequence analysis data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The cct5 mutation also induces nonsense-mediated decay of the mRNA.
source: The mutation also induces nonsense-mediated decay of the mRNA (not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data (not shown in manuscript).

claim: U762 and cct5hi2972bTg mutations failed to complement.
source: U762 and cct5hi2972bTg mutations failed to complement (not shown) supporting the conclusion that the cct5 mutation in U762 is responsible for the tcf7l1a modifier phenotype.
evidence: This claim is supported by complementation test data (not shown in manuscript).

claim: The cct5 mutation in U762 is responsible for the tcf7l1a modifier phenotype.
source: U762 and cct5hi2972bTg mutations failed to complement (not shown) supporting the conclusion that the cct5 mutation in U762 is responsible for the tcf7l1a modifier phenotype.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the complementation test result.

claim: Cct5 is one of the eight subunits of the chaperonin TRiC/TCP-1 protein chaperone complex.
source: Cct5 is one of the eight subunits of the chaperonin TRiC/TCP-1 protein chaperone complex, which assists the folding of actin, tubulin and many proteins involved in cell cycle regulation (Sternlicht et al., 1993; Dekker et al., 2008; Yam et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Sternlicht et al., 1993; Dekker et al., 2008; Yam et al., 2008).

claim: The chaperonin TRiC/TCP-1 protein chaperone complex assists the folding of actin, tubulin and many proteins involved in cell cycle regulation.
source: Cct5 is one of the eight subunits of the chaperonin TRiC/TCP-1 protein chaperone complex, which assists the folding of actin, tubulin and many proteins involved in cell cycle regulation (Sternlicht et al., 1993; Dekker et al., 2008; Yam et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Sternlicht et al., 1993; Dekker et al., 2008; Yam et al., 2008).

claim: Double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a homozygous mutant eyes did not grow beyond 36hpf.
source: Compared to single cct5U762 or tcf7l1a mutants, double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a homozygous mutant eyes did not grow beyond 36hpf (Figure 8 compare D, I to B. G, Figure 8K, dotted line, Supplementary file 1O).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 8 and Supplementary file 1O.

claim: Dying cells were observed in 36hpf and 48hpf cct5U762and cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutant eyes and tecta.
source: As described for other cct gene mutants (Matsuda and Mishina, 2004), we observed dying cells in 36hpf and 48hpf cct5U762and cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutant eyes and tecta (Figure 8—figure supplement 2C), whereas dying cells were rarely detected in these regions at these times in wildtype or Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant siblings (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2 and citation to Matsuda and Mishina, 2004.

claim: Dying cells were rarely detected in the eyes and tecta of wildtype or Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant siblings at 36hpf and 48hpf.
source: As described for other cct gene mutants (Matsuda and Mishina, 2004), we observed dying cells in 36hpf and 48hpf cct5U762and cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutant eyes and tecta (Figure 8—figure supplement 2C), whereas dying cells were rarely detected in these regions at these times in wildtype or Ztcf7l1a-/- mutant siblings (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2.

claim: Double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutants with abrogated Tp53 function showed little or no apoptosis in the eye or tectum.
source: Double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutants with abrogated Tp53 function showed little or no apoptosis in the eye or tectum (Figure 8, compare J to I, arrows; Figure 8—figure supplement 2E,J,O) but still showed eye size reduced similarly to cct5/Ztcf7l1a mutants at 36hpf and 52hpf (Figure 8E,J,K; Supplementary file 1O).
evidence: This claim is supported by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 8 and Figure 8—figure supplement 2E,J,O.

claim: Double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutants with abrogated Tp53 function still showed eye size reduced similarly to cct5/Ztcf7l1a mutants at 36hpf and 52hpf.
source: Double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a mutants with abrogated Tp53 function showed little or no apoptosis in the eye or tectum (Figure 8, compare J to I, arrows; Figure 8—figure supplement 2E,J,O) but still showed eye size reduced similarly to cct5/Ztcf7l1a mutants at 36hpf and 52hpf (Figure 8E,J,K; Supplementary file 1O).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 8E,J,K and Supplementary file 1O.

claim: cct5U762 mutants showed no significant difference in PH3 +cells compared to wildtype siblings.
source: cct5U762 mutants showed no significant difference in PH3 +cells compared to wildtype siblings (Figure 8L,N,P, Supplementary file 1Q, n = 9), whereas double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants showed a 48% increase compared to single Ztcf7l1a mutants (Figure 8M,O,P, Supplementary file 1Q, n = 10, p<0.0051, unpaired t-test, two experiments).
evidence: This claim is supported by PH3 quantification data shown in Figure 8L,N,P and Supplementary file 1Q.

claim: Double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants showed a 48% increase in PH3+ cells compared to single Ztcf7l1a mutants.
source: cct5U762 mutants showed no significant difference in PH3 +cells compared to wildtype siblings (Figure 8L,N,P, Supplementary file 1Q, n = 9), whereas double cct5U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants showed a 48% increase compared to single Ztcf7l1a mutants (Figure 8M,O,P, Supplementary file 1Q, n = 10, p<0.0051, unpaired t-test, two experiments).
evidence: This claim is supported by PH3 quantification data shown in Figure 8M,O,P and Supplementary file 1Q.

claim: By 48hpf, wildtype eyes show strong atoh7:GFP expression in the retinal ganglion cell layer.
source: By 48hpf, wildtype eyes show strong atoh7:GFP expression in the retinal ganglion cell layer (Figure 8—figure supplement 3A, n = 4, arrow head; Masai et al., 2003), whereas although cct5U762/U762 eye cells do express GFP, lamination of neurons is abnormal (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, n = 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3A and citation to Masai et al., 2003.

claim: In cct5U762/U762 eyes, although cells do express GFP, lamination of neurons is abnormal.
source: By 48hpf, wildtype eyes show strong atoh7:GFP expression in the retinal ganglion cell layer (Figure 8—figure supplement 3A, n = 4, arrow head; Masai et al., 2003), whereas although cct5U762/U762 eye cells do express GFP, lamination of neurons is abnormal (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B, n = 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3B.

claim: In cct5U762/U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes, GFP-expressing neurons are almost completely restricted to the ventro-nasal retina.
source: In cct5U762/U762/Ztcf7l1a-/- eyes, GFP-expressing neurons are almost completely restricted to the ventro-nasal retina (Figure 8—figure supplement 3C, n = 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Homozygous U768 mutants show slightly smaller and misshapen eyes.
source: Homozygous U768 mutants show slightly smaller (Figure 9A,C,M, Supplementary file 1R, n = 6, p=0.0143, unpaired t-test) and misshapen eyes; this mutation was mapped to gdf6a (Valdivia et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 9A,C,M and Supplementary file 1R, and citation to Valdivia et al., 2016.

claim: The U768 mutation was mapped to gdf6a.
source: Homozygous U768 mutants show slightly smaller (Figure 9A,C,M, Supplementary file 1R, n = 6, p=0.0143, unpaired t-test) and misshapen eyes; this mutation was mapped to gdf6a (Valdivia et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Valdivia et al., 2016.

claim: Eyes in gdf6aU768/U768/Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos at 36hpf were reduced to 52% the size of eyes in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants.
source: Eyes in gdf6aU768/U768/Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos at 36hpf were reduced to 52% the size of eyes in Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants (Figure 9B,D,M, Supplementary file 1R, n = 3, p=0.0036, unpaired t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by eye volume quantification data shown in Figure 9B,D,M and Supplementary file 1R.

claim: Eyes in gdf6aU768/U768/Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos remained smaller than in single mutants or wildtypes at 52hpf.
source: Unlike Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants in which eye size recovered, eyes in gdf6aU768/U768/Ztcf7l1a-/- embryos remained smaller than in single mutants or wildtypes at 52hpf (Figure 9E–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by imaging data shown in Figure 9E-H.

claim: The ability to compensate eye size is compromised in absence of both gdf6a and tcf7l1a function.
source: This suggests that the ability to compensate eye size is compromised in absence of both gdf6a and tcf7l1a function.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that gdf6a/tcf7l1a double mutant eyes remain smaller and do not recover size.

claim: gdf6a-/- eye fields were reduced to 63% of wildtype size at 10hpf.
source: Volumetric analysis of rx3 expression by fluorescent in situ hybridisation showed that gdf6a-/- eye fields were reduced to 63% of wildtype size at 10hpf (Figure 9I,K,N, arrowheads; Supplementary file 1S, n = 8, p=0.0001, unpaired t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric analysis data shown in Figure 9I,K,N and Supplementary file 1S.

claim: gdf6aU768/U768/Ztcf7l1a-/- eye fields were about ~68% of the size of Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants at 10hpf.
source: Moreover, gdf6aU768/U768/Ztcf7l1a-/- eye fields were about ~68% of the size of Ztcf7l1a-/- mutants (Figure 9I–L,N, arrowheads; Supplementary file 1S, n = 4, p=0.0143, unpaired t-test).
evidence: This claim is supported by volumetric analysis data shown in Figure 9I-L,N and Supplementary file 1S.

claim: Although abrogation of Tcf7l1a function alone has little effect on formation of eyes, it can lead to complete loss of eye formation or more severe eye phenotypes in combination with additional mutations.
source: Altogether, analysis of the interacting mutations reveals that although abrogation of Tcf7l1a function alone has little effect on formation of eyes, it can lead to complete loss of eye formation or more severe eye phenotypes in combination with additional mutations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the analysis of hesx1, cct5, and gdf6a mutations in combination with tcf7l1a.

claim: Although eye development is sufficiently robust to cope with loss of Tcf7l1a, mutant embryos are sensitised to the effects of additional mutations.
source: Consequently, although eye development is sufficiently robust to cope with loss of Tcf7l1a, mutant embryos are sensitised to the effects of additional mutations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that tcf7l1a mutants show enhanced phenotypes when combined with other mutations.
